citations.description: TokenRedactingFilter exists in the repo but repo presence does not confirm prod deployment
TOKEN_HEADER = 'X-Rebar-Token' exists in repo but does not confirm running container state
Ticket body states the container was built 2026-08-04T11:07Z BEFORE 1384 merged ~12:47, and explicitly warns the code is not yet deployed — no subsequent codebase evidence refutes this

findings.criterion: 66af code deployed to the prod box; running container confirmed to source the token from the X-Rebar-Token header and to carry TokenRedactingFilter (no `?token=` URL read).
findings.detail: This criterion requires confirmation that the 66af code is running in the live production container on i-00880b2c7f13527c5. The code changes (TokenRedactingFilter in config.py, X-Rebar-Token header in app.py) are present in the repository, but the criterion explicitly demands confirmation of the *running container* state — a deployment act outside the codebase. No codebase evidence can confirm the prod container has been rebuilt and restarted with the current main. The criterion is untagged and therefore codebase-verifiable by rule, but the required evidence (live container state) is not present in the repository.
findings.remediation: Tag this criterion `[operator-attested]` and record a concrete attestation in a ticket comment naming: the deploy timestamp, the container image digest or build SHA, and a console/log excerpt confirming TokenRedactingFilter and X-Rebar-Token header are active in the running container on i-00880b2c7f13527c5.

citations.description: Ticket comment (2026-08-04): 'The operator running this session attested directly that all affected credentials in this incident have been rotated and all leaked material purged.' — no reference ID, no SSM version, no Gerrit change for webhooks.config push, no rotation timestamp beyond the date.

findings.criterion: Token rotated via service-user.sh: new value is the bot's Gerrit HTTP password, in SSM, and in the pushed webhooks.config; old (compromised) value no longer accepted.
findings.detail: Token rotation is a pure infrastructure/operational act (Gerrit account password change, AWS SSM parameter update, webhooks.config push to refs/meta/config). None of these are verifiable from the repository. The criterion is untagged and therefore codebase-verifiable by rule, but no codebase artifact can confirm SSM parameter values, Gerrit HTTP password state, or that the old token is revoked. The ticket comment attests rotation is complete but names no verifiable specifics (no SSM parameter version, no Gerrit change ID for the webhooks.config push, no timestamp of the actual rotation command).
findings.remediation: Tag this criterion `[operator-attested]` and record a concrete attestation naming: the AWS SSM PutParameter request ID or parameter version number for /rebar/prod/gerrit-bot-token, the Gerrit change ID for the webhooks.config push to refs/meta/config, and the date/time the rotation was executed.

citations.description: Ticket comment attests rotation is complete but provides no evidence of end-to-end verification: no Gerrit change that received a post-rotation LLM-Review vote, no /rerun invocation log, no container restart timestamp.

findings.criterion: review-bot restarted and verified: an inbound webhook/`/rerun` triggers a review AND an outbound LLM-Review vote lands with the new credential.
findings.detail: End-to-end live verification (inbound webhook triggering a review, outbound LLM-Review vote succeeding) is inherently outside the codebase. The criterion is untagged and therefore codebase-verifiable by rule, but no repository artifact can confirm a live webhook was received and processed, or that an outbound vote succeeded with the new credential. The ticket comment contains no specific evidence of this verification (no Gerrit change number that received a vote, no log excerpt, no timestamp of the test run).
findings.remediation: Tag this criterion `[operator-attested]` and record a concrete attestation naming: the Gerrit change number that received a post-rotation LLM-Review vote (with vote timestamp), and/or a log excerpt from the restarted container showing a successful inbound webhook and outbound vote with the new credential.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: for each one, decide whether the work is genuinely incomplete or simply undocumented. If a requirement is already satisfied but the proof is not discoverable from the code alone, add a comment to this ticket that documents the evidence — cite the concrete artifacts that meet the requirement (file paths and line ranges, commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the work to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. For any criterion whose work is genuinely unfinished, complete it, then re-verify.
